title: Plot the Numbers Instead of Tokenizing Them
hook: Feeding a multivariate time series to an LLM as text explodes into thousands of float tokens. Render it as a 2D plot and hand it to a VLM instead: 3.6–10.4x fewer input tokens, and better accuracy.
key_points: LLM inference accounts for over 90% of AI operational energy, and it scales directly with input token count.
Raw multivariate KPI windows from 4G/5G cell sites expand into thousands of floating-point tokens as text.
Encoding the series as 2D plots for a VLM cut input tokens 3.6–10.4x across Llama-3.2-90B, Qwen2.5-VL-72B, and Pixtral-12B.
That translated to 1.8–2.5x measured inference energy reduction — about 7.2 MJ/day at a deployment monitoring 200 cells per 15-minute interval.
Accuracy improved rather than degraded: a fine-tuned Llama-3.2-90B-Vision reached 220.7% higher precision than its text-only counterpart on telecom anomaly detection.
At 24 KPIs, text representations exceed the 128K context window of most production LLMs, while the visual representation still fits.
content_html: There's a mismatch at the heart of using LLMs for numerical monitoring data: a window of multivariate KPIs is a compact numerical object, but tokenizing it as text turns every value into a run of floating-point tokens. Jalli and colleagues, working on telecom network analytics over 4G/5G cell-site data, take the mismatch seriously — LLM inference accounts for over 90% of AI operational energy and scales directly with input token count, so this is an energy problem as much as a context problem.
extra_html:
The swap

Render the time series as a 2D plot and give it to a vision-language model. Across Llama-3.2-90B, Qwen2.5-VL-72B, and Pixtral-12B, that cut input tokens by 3.6–10.4x, and measured inference energy by 1.8–2.5x — roughly 7.2 MJ/day at an edge or CloudRAN deployment monitoring 200 cells every 15 minutes.

The part that isn't a trade-off

Efficiency results usually come with an accuracy cost, and this one doesn't. A fine-tuned Llama-3.2-90B-Vision reported 220.7% higher precision than its text-only counterpart on telecom anomaly detection, and beat LSTM and ARIMA baselines by over 144%; on public benchmarks Pixtral-12B showed a 20.6x improvement in J/F1 score at a mean F1 of 0.82. There's also a hard feasibility argument underneath: at 24 KPIs the text representation blows past the 128K context window most production LLMs offer, so text-only processing requires truncation, while the plot still fits comfortably. The authors' broader pitch is to treat energy consumption as a first-class engineering constraint when choosing an input modality at all.

related.title: Rate-Utility Frontiers for Language Encodings: Comparing Tokens, Bytes, and Pixels
related.hook: Tokens, bytes, or pixels — which encodes language best? A controlled head-to-head across 13 languages finds no single winner: each encoding trades off differently by task.

related.title: Model Routing Is Simple. Until It Isn't.
related.hook: Picking the 'right' model per query looks like classification. IBM Research argues it's really a systems-optimization problem — and treating it as less costs money and speed.

flashcards.prompt: Why does rendering a time series as a plot save so many tokens?
flashcards.back_html: As text, every value in a multivariate window becomes its own run of floating-point tokens — thousands of them. As an image, the same window is a fixed, small number of visual tokens regardless of how many data points it contains.

flashcards.prompt: What happened to accuracy when the numerical data was passed as plots instead of text?

choices.text: It improved — a fine-tuned Llama-3.2-90B-Vision reached 220.7% higher precision than the text-only model on telecom anomaly detection
It dropped modestly, which the paper argues is an acceptable trade for the energy savings
It was unchanged; only the energy cost differed

flashcards.explanation_html: The paper's central claim is that this is not an efficiency-for-accuracy trade: the visual representation was both cheaper and more accurate, also beating LSTM and ARIMA baselines by over 144%.

flashcards.prompt: At 24 KPIs, what makes text-only processing infeasible?
flashcards.back_html: The text representation exceeds the 128K context window of most production LLMs, so you'd have to truncate. The visual representation of the same data stays within standard limits.
